text: Which in-town ski jumping hill, named after a Norwegian stonemason, has trained dozens of Olympians?
hint: In a ranching ski town of the Yampa Valley.
facts: 🎿 Named after Carl Howelsen, who brought ski jumping to town
⛷️ Opened in 1915
🏅 The town has produced dozens of winter Olympians

text: Where is one of the world's largest artificial ski jumps, a stop on the Continental Cup each winter?
hint: An Upper Peninsula iron mining town on the border of the Badger State.
facts: 🎿 Built in 1938
🏆 Hosts an international ski jumping tournament every winter
🏗️ Among the tallest artificial ski jumps in the world

text: Where is the Pipeline, the reef break that hosts the Pipe Masters?
hint: A wave breaking over shallow reef on the North Shore of an island.
facts: 🌊 Waves break over a shallow lava reef
🏆 The Pipe Masters has been held here since 1971
🏖️ Breaks off Ehukai Beach Park

text: Where is 'The Eddie', the big wave contest that runs only when the surf is huge?
hint: A bay on the North Shore where big wave surfing was born in the 1950s.
facts: 🏄 Honours lifeguard Eddie Aikau, lost at sea in 1978
🌊 Held only about ten times since 1984
🤿 Calm in summer, when swimmers leap off its big rock

text: Where is Mavericks, the cold-water big wave break where Mark Foo died in 1994?
hint: Off a harbor village on the coast south of the Golden Gate.
facts: 🌊 Winter waves can top 50 feet
🏄 Jeff Clark surfed it alone for years before others came
🦈 Great white sharks frequent the waters

text: Next to which pier is the U.S. Open of Surfing held every summer?
hint: A long pier in a south coast beach city that calls itself 'Surf City'.
facts: 🌊 The pier is about 1,850 feet long
🏛️ The Surfing Walk of Fame is just across the street
🏄 Duke Kahanamoku surfed here in the 1920s

text: Where is 'Jaws', the giant wave where tow-in surfing was pioneered?
hint: Below the cliffs on the north shore of the Valley Isle.
facts: 🚤 Laird Hamilton and friends pioneered tow-in surfing here in the 1990s
🌊 Winter waves can reach 60 feet
🏆 Has hosted big wave contests of the World Surf League

text: Where is the cobblestone point break named after old railroad bridges, host of the World Surf League Finals?
hint: Inside a state beach next to a big Marine Corps base on the south coast.
facts: 🚂 Named after the wooden railroad trestles over San Mateo Creek
🏆 Hosted the WSL Finals from 2021
🏝️ Part of San Onofre State Beach

text: Where does the world's oldest annual marathon start, every Patriots' Day?
hint: A small town about 26 miles west of the finish line.
facts: 🏁 The race has started here since 1924
📅 The first race was run in 1897
🏃‍♀️ Bobbi Gibb hid in bushes near the start in 1966 to run unofficially

text: Which bridge do tens of thousands of runners cross at the start of the world's largest marathon?
hint: A suspension bridge between two boroughs at the mouth of a great harbor.
facts: 🌉 Opened in 1964, the world's longest suspension span until 1981
🏃 The marathon starts on its Staten Island end
🏅 More than 50,000 runners finish the race each year

text: Which famous flag-raising statue marks the finish of 'the People's Marathon'?
hint: Across the river from the capital, depicting a 1945 scene on Iwo Jima.
facts: 🗿 Depicts the raising of the flag on Iwo Jima in 1945
🏃 The Marine Corps Marathon finishes uphill beside it
🏅 The marathon offers no prize money

text: Where does the 135-mile ultramarathon billed as 'the world's toughest foot race' begin?
hint: The lowest point in North America, 282 feet below sea level.
facts: 🌡️ The race is run in July, in temperatures that can top 120°F
⛰️ It finishes at Whitney Portal, high on Mount Whitney
🧂 The basin floor is a vast salt flat

text: Where is 'the Daddy of 'em All', the world's largest outdoor rodeo, held every July?
hint: In the capital of the Cowboy State, on the high plains.
facts: 🤠 First held in 1897
🐎 Held at Frontier Park
✈️ The Air Force Thunderbirds perform during the event
